idiom_name: multiple return values (T, error) with explicit if err != nil propagation
implementation_notes: Go models effects with values, not with a type constructor: a step returns (T, error) and the caller propagates with 'if err != nil { return nil, err }', which is the language's short-circuit. Generics (Go 1.18) allow a hand-written Result[T] with Map/Chain methods, but there is no higher-kinded polymorphism, so one container cannot serve as the abstract bind for different effect types, and method chaining is not the community idiom. The Go team has repeatedly declined syntactic support (check/handle, try, ?), so the language-appropriate replacement stays explicit error returns, enriched with %w wrapping and batched with helpers such as cmp.Or.
alternative: explicit (T, error) returns with 'if err != nil' propagation - wrap with fmt.Errorf("%w"), batch independent checks with cmp.Or, and keep pipelines as straight-line code.
pitfalls: Discarding the second value ('user, _ :=') drops the effect silently; nothing in the type system forces the check.
%w wrapping is what makes errors.Is/As work; wrapping with %v at a boundary destroys the chain.

A hand-rolled generic Result[T] fights the language and its tooling: it hides the early return readers and linters expect, and it cannot express the absence/async distinction without generics gymnastics.
